newsitem.title: CANADA: Canbra says Pocklington unit to make bid.
newsitem.headline: Canbra says Pocklington unit to make bid.

text.p: Canbra Foods Ltd said on Friday that Hartford Securities Inc, a wholly owned unit of Pocklington Financial (1996) Corp, made a proposal under which it will make a takeover offer for all of Canbra's shares.

The face value of the proposal is C$21 per share, a premium of about 45 percent over the average trading price of Canbra for the 20 days preceding the announcement of a possible transaction on September 19.
A special committee of Canbra's board determined that the offer was fair and recommended that shareholders other than Hartford tender their shares to the offer.
Under the proposal, each Canbra share not held by Hartford would be converted into one $18 Class A redeemable preference share of the merged entity.

These preference shares would be redeemable for C$18 in cash immediately after the amalgamation. Shareholders would also receive one C$3 Class B six percent percent cumulative redeemable preference share of the amalgamated company, to be redeemed no later than December 31, 1999 -- or earlier at the option of the amalgamated company -- for C$3 cash.
Under the proposed transaction, Canbra would become a wholly owned subsidiary of Pocklington.
Hartford now owns 53 percent of the issued and outstanding common shares of Canbra.
The Canbra board named a special committee of independent directors to consider the proposal.
Financial adviser Midland Walwyn Capital Inc delivered its opinion that Canbra shares were worth from C$20.50 to C$24.75 and that the value of the bid was in the range of C$20.50 to C$20.75.
Midland Walwyn said the terms of the deal were fair, from a financial point of view, to the minority shareholders of Canbra.
The special committee concluded that the amalgamation proposal was in the best interests of Canbra and was fair to the shareholders of Canbra, other than Hartford.

It also recommended that the board should authorize Canbra to enter into the agreements necessary to effect the amalgamation proposal and the board should recommend that the shareholders of Canbra vote in favor of the amalgamation proposal.
